i18n.en: The product reuses or references memory after it has been freed. At some point afterward, the memory may be allocated again and saved in another pointer, while the original pointer references a location somewhere within the new allocation. Any operations using the original pointer are no longer valid because the memory "belongs" to the code that operates on the new pointer.

it.en: The program uses memory after freeing it; the attacker fills that freed slot with their data to hijack execution.
it.ar: يستخدم البرنامج الذاكرة بعد تحريرها؛ يملأ المهاجم تلك الخانة المحرَّرة ببياناته ليَخطف التنفيذ.

ot.en: A dangling pointer/reference in the controller is reused, letting crafted data steer the PLC into attacker-chosen behavior.
ot.ar: مؤشّر/مرجع معلّق في المتحكم يُعاد استخدامه، فتوجّه بيانات مُعدّة الـPLC إلى سلوك يختاره المهاجم.

i18n.en: The product uses a primary channel for administration or restricted functionality, but it does not properly protect the channel.
The product protects a primary channel, but it does not use the same level of protection for an alternate channel.

CWE-421.name: Race Condition During Access to Alternate Channel

i18n.en: The product opens an alternate channel to communicate with an authorized user, but the channel is accessible to other actors.

The product does not properly verify the source of a message in the Windows Messaging System while running at elevated privileges, creating an alternate channel through which an attacker can directly send a message to the product.
This entry has been deprecated because it was a duplicate of CWE-441. All content has been transferred to CWE-441.
The product does not sufficiently protect all possible paths that a user can take to access restricted functionality or resources.
The web application does not adequately enforce appropriate authorization on all restricted URLs, scripts, or files.

it.en: A hidden admin page has no access check, so the attacker who guesses the URL reaches it directly (forced browsing).
it.ar: صفحة إدارة مخفية بلا فحص وصول، فمن يخمّن رابطها من المهاجمين يصل إليها مباشرة (تصفّح قسري).

i18n.en: The product searches for critical resources using an externally-supplied search path that can point to resources that are not under the product's direct control.
The product uses a fixed or controlled search path to find resources, but one or more locations in that path can be under the control of unintended actors.
The product uses a search path that contains an unquoted element, in which the element contains whitespace or other separators. This can cause the product to access resources in a parent path.
The wrong "handler" is assigned to process an object.
A handler is not available or implemented.

CWE-432.name: Dangerous Signal Handler not Disabled During Sensitive Operations

i18n.en: The product uses a signal handler that shares state with other signal handlers, but it does not properly mask or prevent those signal handlers from being invoked while the original signal handler is still running.
The product stores raw content or supporting code under the web document root with an extension that is not specifically handled by the server.

CWE-434.name: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type

i18n.en: The product allows the upload or transfer of dangerous file types that are automatically processed within its environment.

it.en: The attacker uploads a .php/.jsp 'image'; the server stores it in a runnable folder and executes it as a web shell.
it.ar: يرفع المهاجم 'صورة' بصيغة .php/.jsp؛ يخزّنها الخادم في مجلد قابل للتشغيل وينفّذها كصدفة ويب.

CWE-435.name: Improper Interaction Between Multiple Correctly-Behaving Entities

i18n.en: An interaction error occurs when two entities have correct behavior when running independently of each other, but when they are integrated as components in a larger system or process, they introduce incorrect behaviors that may cause resultant weaknesses.
i18n.ar: تفاعل غير سليم بين كيانات متعددة سليمة السلوك يؤدي إلى ثغرة.

i18n.en: Product A handles inputs or steps differently than Product B, which causes A to perform incorrect actions based on its perception of B's state.
i18n.ar: تعارض في تفسير البيانات بين مكوّنين مختلفين.

i18n.en: A product acts as an intermediary or monitor between two or more endpoints, but it does not have a complete model of an endpoint's features, behaviors, or state, potentially causing the product to perform incorrect actions based on this incomplete model.

CWE-439.name: Behavioral Change in New Version or Environment

i18n.en: A's behavior or functionality changes with a new version of A, or a new environment, which is not known (or manageable) by B.
A feature, API, or function does not perform according to its specification.

The product receives a request, message, or directive from an upstream component, but the product does not sufficiently preserve the original source of the request before forwarding the request to an external actor that is outside of the product's control sphere. This causes the product to appear to be the source of the request, leading it to act as a proxy or other intermediary between the upstream component and the external actor.
i18n.ar: وسيط أو بروكسي غير مقصود («النائب المخدوع») ينفّذ طلبات نيابة عن المهاجم.

i18n.en: This weakness can be found at CWE-113.

CWE-444.name: Inconsistent Interpretation of HTTP Requests ('HTTP Request/Response Smuggling')

i18n.en: The product acts as an intermediary HTTP agent (such as a proxy or firewall) in the data flow between two entities such as a client and server, but it does not interpret malformed HTTP requests or responses in ways that are consistent with how the messages will be processed by those entities that are at the ultimate destination.
The user interface does not correctly enable or configure a security feature, but the interface provides feedback that causes the user to believe that the feature is in a secure state.

CWE-447.name: Unimplemented or Unsupported Feature in UI

i18n.en: A UI function for a security feature appears to be supported and gives feedback to the user that suggests that it is supported, but the underlying functionality is not implemented.
A UI function is obsolete and the product does not warn the user.

CWE-449.name: The UI Performs the Wrong Action

i18n.en: The UI performs the wrong action with respect to the user's request.
The UI has multiple interpretations of user input but does not prompt the user when it selects the less secure interpretation.

CWE-451.name: User Interface (UI) Misrepresentation of Critical Information

i18n.en: The user interface (UI) does not properly represent critical information to the user, allowing the information - or its source - to be obscured or spoofed. This is often a component in phishing attacks.
The product, by default, initializes an internal variable with an insecure or less secure value than is possible.

CWE-454.name: External Initialization of Trusted Variables or Data Stores

i18n.en: The product initializes critical internal variables or data stores using inputs that can be modified by untrusted actors.

The product does not exit or otherwise modify its operation when security-relevant errors occur during initialization, such as when a configuration file has a format error or a hardware security module (HSM) cannot be activated, which can cause the product to execute in a less secure fashion than intended by the administrator.
The product does not initialize critical variables, which causes the execution environment to use unexpected values.
The code uses a variable that has not been initialized, leading to unpredictable or unintended results.

ot.en: A variable is read before it's set, so the controller acts on leftover/garbage memory — unpredictable, unsafe output.
ot.ar: يُقرأ متغيّر قبل ضبطه، فيتصرّف المتحكم بناءً على ذاكرة متبقّية/عشوائية — مخرَج غير متوقع وغير آمن.

it.en: Using a variable before it's initialized makes behavior depend on leftover memory, which an attacker can influence.
it.ar: استخدام متغيّر قبل تهيئته يجعل السلوك يعتمد على ذاكرة متبقّية يمكن للمهاجم التأثير فيها.

i18n.en: This weakness has been deprecated because its name and description did not match. The description duplicated CWE-454, while the name suggested a more abstract initialization problem. Please refer to CWE-665 for the more abstract problem.
The product does not properly "clean up" and remove temporary or supporting resources after they have been used.
The product does not clean up its state or incorrectly cleans up its state when an exception is thrown, leading to unexpected state or control flow.
Duplicate keys in associative lists can lead to non-unique keys being mistaken for an error.
The accidental deletion of a data-structure sentinel can cause serious programming logic problems.
The accidental addition of a data-structure sentinel can cause serious programming logic problems.

CWE-466.name: Return of Pointer Value Outside of Expected Range

i18n.en: A function can return a pointer to memory that is outside of the buffer that the pointer is expected to reference.

CWE-467.name: Use of sizeof() on a Pointer Type

i18n.en: The code calls sizeof() on a pointer type, which can be an incorrect calculation if the programmer intended to determine the size of the data that is being pointed to.
In C and C++, one may often accidentally refer to the wrong memory due to the semantics of when math operations are implicitly scaled.

CWE-469.name: Use of Pointer Subtraction to Determine Size

i18n.en: The product subtracts one pointer from another in order to determine size, but this calculation can be incorrect if the pointers do not exist in the same memory chunk.

CWE-470.name: Use of Externally-Controlled Input to Select Classes or Code ('Unsafe Reflection')

i18n.en: The product uses external input with reflection to select which classes or code to use, but it does not sufficiently prevent the input from selecting improper classes or code.
The product does not properly protect an assumed-immutable element from being modified by an attacker.

it.en: The attacker overwrites a value the program trusts (e.g. an array length or flag), changing logic the developer assumed fixed.
it.ar: يطمس المهاجم قيمة يثق بها البرنامج (مثل طول مصفوفة أو علم)، فيغيّر منطقًا افترضه المطوّر ثابتًا.

CWE-472.name: External Control of Assumed-Immutable Web Parameter

i18n.en: The web application does not sufficiently verify inputs that are assumed to be immutable but are actually externally controllable, such as hidden form fields.

A PHP application does not properly protect against the modification of variables from external sources, such as query parameters or cookies. This can expose the application to numerous weaknesses that would not exist otherwise.

CWE-474.name: Use of Function with Inconsistent Implementations

i18n.en: The code uses a function that has inconsistent implementations across operating systems and versions.

CWE-475.name: Undefined Behavior for Input to API

i18n.en: The behavior of this function is undefined unless its control parameter is set to a specific value.
The product dereferences a pointer that it expects to be valid but is NULL.

it.en: The attacker triggers a null value where the code expects an object, crashing the service (denial of service).
it.ar: يُطلق المهاجم قيمة فارغة حيث تتوقع الشيفرة كائنًا، فيُعطّل الخدمة (حجب خدمة).

ot.en: A null/invalid reference is dereferenced in the controller, faulting the CPU and stopping the process scan.
ot.ar: يُفكّ مرجع فارغ/غير صالح في المتحكم، فيتعطّل المعالج وتتوقف دورة العملية.

i18n.en: The code uses deprecated or obsolete functions, which suggests that the code has not been actively reviewed or maintained.

CWE-478.name: Missing Default Case in Multiple Condition Expression

i18n.en: The code does not have a default case in an expression with multiple conditions, such as a switch statement.

CWE-479.name: Signal Handler Use of a Non-reentrant Function

i18n.en: The product defines a signal handler that calls a non-reentrant function.
The product accidentally uses the wrong operator, which changes the logic in security-relevant ways.
The code uses an operator for assignment when the intention was to perform a comparison.
The code uses an operator for comparison when the intention was to perform an assignment.
The code does not explicitly delimit a block that is intended to contain 2 or more statements, creating a logic error.

The product omits a break statement within a switch or similar construct, causing code associated with multiple conditions to execute. This can cause problems when the programmer only intended to execute code associated with one condition.
The product compares classes by name, which can cause it to use the wrong class when multiple classes can have the same name.
Java packages are not inherently closed; therefore, relying on them for code security is not a good practice.

CWE-488.name: Exposure of Data Element to Wrong Session

i18n.en: The product does not sufficiently enforce boundaries between the states of different sessions, causing data to be provided to, or used by, the wrong session.
The product is released with debugging code still enabled or active.

it.en: Debug/test code left enabled gives the attacker verbose internals or backdoor actions in production.
it.ar: شيفرة تنقيح/اختبار تُركت مفعّلة تمنح المهاجم تفاصيل داخلية مطوّلة أو إجراءات خلفية في الإنتاج.

CWE-491.name: Public cloneable() Method Without Final ('Object Hijack')

i18n.en: A class has a cloneable() method that is not declared final, which allows an object to be created without calling the constructor. This can cause the object to be in an unexpected state.

CWE-492.name: Use of Inner Class Containing Sensitive Data

i18n.en: Inner classes are translated into classes that are accessible at package scope and may expose code that the programmer intended to keep private to attackers.

CWE-493.name: Critical Public Variable Without Final Modifier

i18n.en: The product has a critical public variable that is not final, which allows the variable to be modified to contain unexpected values.

CWE-494.name: Download of Code Without Integrity Check

i18n.en: The product downloads source code or an executable from a remote location and executes the code without sufficiently verifying the origin and integrity of the code.

it.en: An update is downloaded without an integrity check, so an attacker swaps it for a malicious one and you install it.
it.ar: يُنزَّل تحديث دون فحص سلامة، فيستبدله المهاجم بآخر خبيث وتثبّته أنت.

ot.en: Firmware/logic is loaded without verifying its signature, letting an attacker push tampered code to the controller.
ot.ar: تُحمَّل البرامج الثابتة/المنطق دون التحقق من توقيعها، فيدفع المهاجم شيفرة معبوثًا بها إلى المتحكم.

CWE-495.name: Private Data Structure Returned From A Public Method

i18n.en: The product has a method that is declared public, but returns a reference to a private data structure, which could then be modified in unexpected ways.

CWE-496.name: Public Data Assigned to Private Array-Typed Field

i18n.en: Assigning public data to a private array is equivalent to giving public access to the array.

CWE-497.name: Exposure of Sensitive System Information to an Unauthorized Control Sphere

i18n.en: The product does not properly prevent sensitive system-level information from being accessed by unauthorized actors who do not have the same level of access to the underlying system as the product does.

it.en: Internal system info (paths, IPs, versions) leaks to the attacker, mapping the network for the next move.
it.ar: تتسرّب معلومات النظام الداخلية (مسارات، عناوين IP، إصدارات) إلى المهاجم، فيرسم خريطة الشبكة لخطوته التالية.

i18n.en: The code contains a class with sensitive data, but the class is cloneable. The data can then be accessed by cloning the class.
The code contains a class with sensitive data, but the class does not explicitly deny serialization. The data can be accessed by serializing the class through another class.

CWE-500.name: Public Static Field Not Marked Final

i18n.en: An object contains a public static field that is not marked final, which might allow it to be modified in unexpected ways.
The product mixes trusted and untrusted data in the same data structure or structured message.
The product deserializes untrusted data without sufficiently ensuring that the resulting data will be valid.
i18n.ar: فك تسلسل بيانات غير موثوقة مما يسمح بحقن كائنات أو شيفرة.

it.en: The attacker sends a crafted serialized object; deserializing it runs attacker code or rebuilds dangerous objects (RCE).
it.ar: يرسل المهاجم كائنًا متسلسلًا مُعدًّا؛ ففكّ تسلسله يشغّل شيفرة المهاجم أو يعيد بناء كائنات خطرة (تنفيذ عن بُعد).

i18n.en: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.

it.en: Hidden malicious logic (a backdoor) in the code lets the attacker who planted it bypass all controls later.
it.ar: منطق خبيث مخفي (باب خلفي) في الشيفرة يتيح لمن زرعه تجاوز كل الضوابط لاحقًا.

i18n.en: The product appears to contain benign or useful functionality, but it also contains code that is hidden from normal operation that violates the intended security policy of the user or the system administrator.
Non-replicating malicious code only resides on the target system or product that is attacked; it does not attempt to spread to other systems.
Replicating malicious code, including viruses and worms, will attempt to attack other systems once it has successfully compromised the target system or the product.
A trapdoor is a hidden piece of code that responds to a special input, allowing its user access to resources without passing through the normal security enforcement mechanism.
The product contains code that is designed to disrupt the legitimate operation of the product (or its environment) when a certain time passes, or when a certain logical condition is met.

ot.en: Logic that triggers on a date/condition (a logic bomb) can sabotage the process at a time the attacker chose.
ot.ar: منطق يُطلَق عند تاريخ/شرط (قنبلة منطقية) قد يخرّب العملية في وقت اختاره المهاجم.

it.en: Time/condition-triggered malicious code activates later to damage data or systems on the attacker's schedule.
it.ar: شيفرة خبيثة تُطلَق بزمن/شرط تنشط لاحقًا لإتلاف البيانات أو الأنظمة وفق جدول المهاجم.

i18n.en: The product collects personally identifiable information about a human user or the user's activities, but the product accesses this information using other resources besides itself, and it does not require that user's explicit approval or direct input into the product.
A covert channel is a path that can be used to transfer information in a way not intended by the system's designers.

A covert storage channel transfers information through the setting of bits by one program and the reading of those bits by another. What distinguishes this case from that of ordinary operation is that the bits are used to convey encoded information.
This weakness can be found at CWE-385.
Allowing a .NET application to run at potentially escalated levels of access to the underlying operating and file systems can be dangerous and result in various forms of attacks.
The product does not require that users should have strong passwords.

it.en: Weak password rules let users (and attackers) set '123456', so accounts fall to simple guessing.
it.ar: قواعد كلمات مرور ضعيفة تتيح ضبط '123456'، فتسقط الحسابات أمام تخمين بسيط.

i18n.en: The product transmits or stores authentication credentials, but it uses an insecure method that is susceptible to unauthorized interception and/or retrieval.
Login pages do not use adequate measures to protect the user name and password while they are in transit from the client to the server.

CWE-524.name: Use of Cache Containing Sensitive Information

i18n.en: The code uses a cache that contains sensitive information, but the cache can be read by an actor outside of the intended control sphere.

CWE-525.name: Use of Web Browser Cache Containing Sensitive Information

i18n.en: The web application does not use an appropriate caching policy that specifies the extent to which each web page and associated form fields should be cached.

CWE-526.name: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information in an Environment Variable

i18n.en: The product uses an environment variable to store unencrypted sensitive information.

CWE-527.name: Exposure of Version-Control Repository to an Unauthorized Control Sphere

i18n.en: The product stores a CVS, git, or other repository in a directory, archive, or other resource that is stored, transferred, or otherwise made accessible to unauthorized actors.

CWE-528.name: Exposure of Core Dump File to an Unauthorized Control Sphere

i18n.en: The product generates a core dump file in a directory, archive, or other resource that is stored, transferred, or otherwise made accessible to unauthorized actors.

CWE-529.name: Exposure of Access Control List Files to an Unauthorized Control Sphere

i18n.en: The product stores access control list files in a directory or other container that is accessible to actors outside of the intended control sphere.

CWE-530.name: Exposure of Backup File to an Unauthorized Control Sphere

i18n.en: A backup file is stored in a directory or archive that is made accessible to unauthorized actors.

CWE-531.name: Inclusion of Sensitive Information in Test Code

i18n.en: Accessible test applications can pose a variety of security risks. Since developers or administrators rarely consider that someone besides themselves would even know about the existence of these applications, it is common for them to contain sensitive information or functions.

CWE-532.name: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

i18n.en: The product writes sensitive information to a log file.

it.en: Passwords/tokens written into log files let anyone who reads the logs reuse those credentials.
it.ar: كتابة كلمات المرور/الرموز في ملفات السجل تتيح لمن يقرأ السجلات إعادة استخدام تلك الاعتمادات.

CWE-533.name: DEPRECATED: Information Exposure Through Server Log Files

i18n.en: This entry has been deprecated because its abstraction was too low-level. See CWE-532.

CWE-534.name: DEPRECATED: Information Exposure Through Debug Log Files

i18n.en: This entry has been deprecated because its abstraction was too low-level. See CWE-532.

CWE-535.name: Exposure of Information Through Shell Error Message

i18n.en: A command shell error message indicates that there exists an unhandled exception in the web application code. In many cases, an attacker can leverage the conditions that cause these errors in order to gain unauthorized access to the system.

CWE-536.name: Servlet Runtime Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

i18n.en: A servlet error message indicates that there exists an unhandled exception in the web application code and may provide useful information to an attacker.

CWE-537.name: Java Runtime Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

i18n.en: In many cases, an attacker can leverage the conditions that cause unhandled exception errors in order to gain unauthorized access to the system.

CWE-538.name: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Externally-Accessible File or Directory

i18n.en: The product places sensitive information into files or directories that are accessible to actors who are allowed to have access to the files, but not to the sensitive information.

CWE-539.name: Use of Persistent Cookies Containing Sensitive Information

i18n.en: The web application uses persistent cookies, but the cookies contain sensitive information.

CWE-540.name: Inclusion of Sensitive Information in Source Code

i18n.en: Source code on a web server or repository often contains sensitive information and should generally not be accessible to users.

CWE-541.name: Inclusion of Sensitive Information in an Include File

i18n.en: If an include file source is accessible, the file can contain usernames and passwords, as well as sensitive information pertaining to the application and system.

CWE-542.name: DEPRECATED: Information Exposure Through Cleanup Log Files

i18n.en: This entry has been deprecated because its abstraction was too low-level. See CWE-532.

CWE-543.name: Use of Singleton Pattern Without Synchronization in a Multithreaded Context

i18n.en: The product uses the singleton pattern when creating a resource within a multithreaded environment.
The product does not use a standardized method for handling errors throughout the code, which might introduce inconsistent error handling and resultant weaknesses.

CWE-545.name: DEPRECATED: Use of Dynamic Class Loading

i18n.en: This weakness has been deprecated because it partially overlaps CWE-470, it describes legitimate programmer behavior, and other portions will need to be integrated into other entries.
The code contains comments that suggest the presence of bugs, incomplete functionality, or weaknesses.
The product uses hard-coded constants instead of symbolic names for security-critical values, which increases the likelihood of mistakes during code maintenance or security policy change.

ot.en: Security values hard-coded as constants (limits, keys) can't be changed or rotated, and an attacker who reads them knows the secret forever.
ot.ar: قيم أمنية مثبّتة كثوابت (حدود، مفاتيح) لا يمكن تغييرها أو تدويرها، ومن يقرأها من المهاجمين يعرف السر للأبد.

CWE-548.name: Exposure of Information Through Directory Listing

i18n.en: The product inappropriately exposes a directory listing with an index of all the resources located inside of the directory.

it.en: Directory listing is on, so the attacker browses the folder and finds backups, configs, and files you didn't link.
it.ar: سرد المجلدات مفعّل، فيتصفّح المهاجم المجلد ويجد نسخًا احتياطية وإعدادات وملفات لم تربطها.

i18n.en: The product does not mask passwords during entry, increasing the potential for attackers to observe and capture passwords.

CWE-550.name: Server-generated Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

i18n.en: Certain conditions, such as network failure, will cause a server error message to be displayed.

CWE-551.name: Incorrect Behavior Order: Authorization Before Parsing and Canonicalization

i18n.en: If a web server does not fully parse requested URLs before it examines them for authorization, it may be possible for an attacker to bypass authorization protection.

CWE-552.name: Files or Directories Accessible to External Parties

i18n.en: The product makes files or directories accessible to unauthorized actors, even though they should not be.

CWE-553.name: Command Shell in Externally Accessible Directory

i18n.en: A possible shell file exists in /cgi-bin/ or other accessible directories. This is extremely dangerous and can be used by an attacker to execute commands on the web server.

CWE-554.name: ASP.NET Misconfiguration: Not Using Input Validation Framework

i18n.en: The ASP.NET application does not use an input validation framework.

CWE-555.name: J2EE Misconfiguration: Plaintext Password in Configuration File

i18n.en: The J2EE application stores a plaintext password in a configuration file.

CWE-556.name: ASP.NET Misconfiguration: Use of Identity Impersonation

i18n.en: Configuring an ASP.NET application to run with impersonated credentials may give the application unnecessary privileges.

CWE-558.name: Use of getlogin() in Multithreaded Application

i18n.en: The product uses the getlogin() function in a multithreaded context, potentially causing it to return incorrect values.

CWE-560.name: Use of umask() with chmod-style Argument

i18n.en: The product calls umask() with an incorrect argument that is specified as if it is an argument to chmod().
The product contains dead code, which can never be executed.

it.en: Dead code isn't a direct attack, but it hides intent and may re-activate an unsafe path during maintenance.
it.ar: الشيفرة الميتة ليست هجومًا مباشرًا، لكنها تُخفي النية وقد تُعيد تفعيل مسار غير آمن أثناء الصيانة.

i18n.en: A function returns the address of a stack variable, which will cause unintended program behavior, typically in the form of a crash.

it.en: Returning a pointer to a local (stack) variable lets later code read freed memory the attacker can fill.
it.ar: إعادة مؤشّر لمتغيّر محلي (مكدّس) تتيح لشيفرة لاحقة قراءة ذاكرة محرَّرة يملؤها المهاجم.

i18n.en: The variable's value is assigned but never used, making it a dead store.
Using Hibernate to execute a dynamic SQL statement built with user-controlled input can allow an attacker to modify the statement's meaning or to execute arbitrary SQL commands.

CWE-565.name: Reliance on Cookies without Validation and Integrity Checking

i18n.en: The product relies on the existence or values of cookies when performing security-critical operations, but it does not properly ensure that the setting is valid for the associated user.

CWE-566.name: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled SQL Primary Key

i18n.en: The product uses a database table that includes records that should not be accessible to an actor, but it executes a SQL statement with a primary key that can be controlled by that actor.

CWE-567.name: Unsynchronized Access to Shared Data in a Multithreaded Context

i18n.en: The product does not properly synchronize shared data, such as static variables across threads, which can lead to undefined behavior and unpredictable data changes.
The product contains a finalize() method that does not call super.finalize().
The product contains an expression that will always evaluate to false.
The product contains an expression that will always evaluate to true.

CWE-572.name: Call to Thread run() instead of start()

i18n.en: The product calls a thread's run() method instead of calling start(), which causes the code to run in the thread of the caller instead of the callee.

CWE-573.name: Improper Following of Specification by Caller

i18n.en: The product does not follow or incorrectly follows the specifications as required by the implementation language, environment, framework, protocol, or platform.

CWE-574.name: EJB Bad Practices: Use of Synchronization Primitives

i18n.en: The product violates the Enterprise JavaBeans (EJB) specification by using thread synchronization primitives.

CWE-575.name: EJB Bad Practices: Use of AWT Swing

i18n.en: The product violates the Enterprise JavaBeans (EJB) specification by using AWT/Swing.

CWE-576.name: EJB Bad Practices: Use of Java I/O

i18n.en: The product violates the Enterprise JavaBeans (EJB) specification by using the java.io package.

CWE-577.name: EJB Bad Practices: Use of Sockets

i18n.en: The product violates the Enterprise JavaBeans (EJB) specification by using sockets.

CWE-578.name: EJB Bad Practices: Use of Class Loader

i18n.en: The product violates the Enterprise JavaBeans (EJB) specification by using the class loader.

CWE-579.name: J2EE Bad Practices: Non-serializable Object Stored in Session

i18n.en: The product stores a non-serializable object as an HttpSession attribute, which can hurt reliability.
The product contains a clone() method that does not call super.clone() to obtain the new object.

CWE-581.name: Object Model Violation: Just One of Equals and Hashcode Defined

i18n.en: The product does not maintain equal hashcodes for equal objects.

CWE-582.name: Array Declared Public, Final, and Static

i18n.en: The product declares an array public, final, and static, which is not sufficient to prevent the array's contents from being modified.
The product violates secure coding principles for mobile code by declaring a finalize() method public.
The code has a return statement inside a finally block, which will cause any thrown exception in the try block to be discarded.
The product contains an empty synchronized block.
The product makes an explicit call to the finalize() method from outside the finalizer.

CWE-587.name: Assignment of a Fixed Address to a Pointer

i18n.en: The product sets a pointer to a specific address other than NULL or 0.

CWE-588.name: Attempt to Access Child of a Non-structure Pointer

i18n.en: Casting a non-structure type to a structure type and accessing a field can lead to memory access errors or data corruption.

The product uses an API function that does not exist on all versions of the target platform. This could cause portability problems or inconsistencies that allow denial of service or other consequences.

CWE-590.name: Free of Memory not on the Heap

i18n.en: The product calls free() on a pointer to memory that was not allocated using associated heap allocation functions such as malloc(), calloc(), or realloc().

it.en: Freeing memory that wasn't heap-allocated corrupts the allocator, which an attacker can steer into code execution.
it.ar: تحرير ذاكرة لم تُحجز من الكومة يُفسد المُخصِّص، ويوجّهه المهاجم نحو تنفيذ شيفرة.

CWE-591.name: Sensitive Data Storage in Improperly Locked Memory

i18n.en: The product stores sensitive data in memory that is not locked, or that has been incorrectly locked, which might cause the memory to be written to swap files on disk by the virtual memory manager. This can make the data more accessible to external actors.
This weakness has been deprecated because it covered redundant concepts already described in CWE-287.

CWE-593.name: Authentication Bypass: OpenSSL CTX Object Modified after SSL Objects are Created

i18n.en: The product modifies the SSL context after connection creation has begun.

CWE-594.name: J2EE Framework: Saving Unserializable Objects to Disk

i18n.en: When the J2EE container attempts to write unserializable objects to disk there is no guarantee that the process will complete successfully.

CWE-595.name: Comparison of Object References Instead of Object Contents

i18n.en: The product compares object references instead of the contents of the objects themselves, preventing it from detecting equivalent objects.

This weakness has been deprecated. It was poorly described and difficult to distinguish from other entries. It was also inappropriate to assign a separate ID solely because of domain-specific considerations. Its closest equivalent is CWE-1023.

CWE-597.name: Use of Wrong Operator in String Comparison

i18n.en: The product uses the wrong operator when comparing a string, such as using "==" when the .equals() method should be used instead.

CWE-598.name: Use of HTTP Request With Sensitive Query String

i18n.en: The web application uses an HTTP method to process a request, but the request includes sensitive information in the query string.
The product uses OpenSSL and trusts or uses a certificate without using the SSL_get_verify_result() function to ensure that the certificate satisfies all necessary security requirements.
The Servlet does not catch all exceptions, which may reveal sensitive debugging information.

CWE-601.name: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

i18n.en: The web application accepts a user-controlled input that specifies a link to an external site, and uses that link in a redirect.
i18n.ar: أخذ وجهة إعادة التوجيه من مدخل غير موثوق دون تحقّق.

it.en: The attacker crafts a link on your trusted domain that redirects victims to a phishing site, abusing your reputation.
it.ar: يصنع المهاجم رابطًا على نطاقك الموثوق يحوّل الضحايا إلى موقع تصيّد، مستغلًّا سمعتك.

i18n.en: The product is composed of a server that relies on the client to implement a mechanism that is intended to protect the server.

A client/server product performs authentication within client code but not in server code, allowing server-side authentication to be bypassed via a modified client that omits the authentication check.

CWE-605.name: Multiple Binds to the Same Port

i18n.en: When multiple sockets are allowed to bind to the same port, other services on that port may be stolen or spoofed.

it.en: Binding the same port twice (or a race on it) lets an attacker hijack the listener and intercept connections.
it.ar: ربط المنفذ نفسه مرتين (أو تسابق عليه) يتيح لمهاجم اختطاف المُستمع واعتراض الاتصالات.

i18n.en: The product does not properly check inputs that are used for loop conditions, potentially leading to a denial of service or other consequences because of excessive looping.

it.en: Unchecked loop input lets the attacker pick a huge count, freezing the program in a long/endless loop.
it.ar: مُدخل حلقة غير مفحوص يتيح للمهاجم اختيار عدد ضخم، فيُجمّد البرنامج في حلقة طويلة/لا نهائية.

ot.en: A wire/HMI value sets a loop count with no cap, so the controller spins past its cycle time and watchdog-faults.
ot.ar: قيمة شبكة/HMI تضبط عدّ الحلقة دون سقف، فيدور المتحكم متجاوزًا زمن دورته ويتعطّل بالمراقب.

CWE-607.name: Public Static Final Field References Mutable Object

i18n.en: A public or protected static final field references a mutable object, which allows the object to be changed by malicious code, or accidentally from another package.

CWE-608.name: Struts: Non-private Field in ActionForm Class

i18n.en: An ActionForm class contains a field that has not been declared private, which can be accessed without using a setter or getter.
The product uses double-checked locking to access a resource without the overhead of explicit synchronization, but the locking is insufficient.

CWE-610.name: Externally Controlled Reference to a Resource in Another Sphere

i18n.en: The product uses an externally controlled name or reference that resolves to a resource that is outside of the intended control sphere.
i18n.ar: تحكّم المدخلات في مرجع يُحَل ضمن نطاق تحكّم آخر.

CWE-611.name: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

i18n.en: The product processes an XML document that can contain XML entities with URIs that resolve to documents outside of the intended sphere of control, causing the product to embed incorrect documents into its output.

it.en: The attacker sends XML that references an external file/URL (XXE), making the server read local secrets or call internal hosts.
it.ar: يرسل المهاجم XML يشير إلى ملف/رابط خارجي (XXE)، فيجعل الخادم يقرأ أسرارًا محلية أو يستدعي مضيفات داخلية.

CWE-612.name: Improper Authorization of Index Containing Sensitive Information

i18n.en: The product creates a search index of private or sensitive documents, but it does not properly limit index access to actors who are authorized to see the original information.
According to WASC, "Insufficient Session Expiration is when a web site permits an attacker to reuse old session credentials or session IDs for authorization."

it.en: Sessions never expire, so a stolen token works forever and a logged-out user is still 'in'.
it.ar: الجلسات لا تنتهي، فيظل رمز مسروق يعمل للأبد ويبقى مستخدم سجّل خروجه 'بالداخل'.

CWE-614.name: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute

i18n.en: The Secure attribute for sensitive cookies in HTTPS sessions is not set.

it.en: A session cookie without the Secure flag is sent over plain HTTP, where an attacker on the network grabs it.
it.ar: ملف ارتباط جلسة بلا علم Secure يُرسَل عبر HTTP غير مشفّر، حيث يلتقطه مهاجم على الشبكة.

CWE-615.name: Inclusion of Sensitive Information in Source Code Comments

i18n.en: While adding general comments is very useful, some programmers tend to leave important data, such as: filenames related to the web application, old links or links which were not meant to be browsed by users, old code fragments, etc.

CWE-616.name: Incomplete Identification of Uploaded File Variables (PHP)

i18n.en: The PHP application uses an old method for processing uploaded files by referencing the four global variables that are set for each file (e.g. $varname, $varname_size, $varname_name, $varname_type). These variables could be overwritten by attackers, causing the application to process unauthorized files.
The product contains an assert() or similar statement that can be triggered by an attacker, which leads to an application exit or other behavior that is more severe than necessary.
An ActiveX control is intended for use in a web browser, but it exposes dangerous methods that perform actions that are outside of the browser's security model (e.g. the zone or domain).
If a database cursor is not closed properly, then it could become accessible to other users while retaining the same privileges that were originally assigned, leaving the cursor "dangling."
When setting a new password for a user, the product does not require knowledge of the original password, or using another form of authentication.

The product uses external input to determine the names of variables into which information is extracted, without verifying that the names of the specified variables are valid. This could cause the program to overwrite unintended variables.

CWE-622.name: Improper Validation of Function Hook Arguments

i18n.en: The product adds hooks to user-accessible API functions, but it does not properly validate the arguments. This could lead to resultant vulnerabilities.

CWE-623.name: Unsafe ActiveX Control Marked Safe For Scripting

i18n.en: An ActiveX control is intended for restricted use, but it has been marked as safe-for-scripting.
The product uses a regular expression that either (1) contains an executable component with user-controlled inputs, or (2) allows a user to enable execution by inserting pattern modifiers.
The product uses a regular expression that does not sufficiently restrict the set of allowed values.

CWE-626.name: Null Byte Interaction Error (Poison Null Byte)

i18n.en: The product does not properly handle null bytes or NUL characters when passing data between different representations or components.

In a language where the user can influence the name of a variable at runtime, if the variable names are not controlled, an attacker can read or write to arbitrary variables, or access arbitrary functions.

CWE-628.name: Function Call with Incorrectly Specified Arguments

i18n.en: The product calls a function, procedure, or routine with arguments that are not correctly specified, leading to always-incorrect behavior and resultant weaknesses.

When the product encounters an error condition or failure, its design requires it to fall back to a state that is less secure than other options that are available, such as selecting the weakest encryption algorithm or using the most permissive access control restrictions.

CWE-637.name: Unnecessary Complexity in Protection Mechanism (Not Using 'Economy of Mechanism')

i18n.en: The product uses a more complex mechanism than necessary, which could lead to resultant weaknesses when the mechanism is not correctly understood, modeled, configured, implemented, or used.

The product does not perform access checks on a resource every time the resource is accessed by an entity, which can create resultant weaknesses if that entity's rights or privileges change over time.
The system's authorization functionality does not prevent one user from gaining access to another user's data or record by modifying the key value identifying the data.

CWE-640.name: Weak Password Recovery Mechanism for Forgotten Password

i18n.en: The product contains a mechanism for users to recover or change their passwords without knowing the original password, but the mechanism is weak.

CWE-641.name: Improper Restriction of Names for Files and Other Resources

i18n.en: The product constructs the name of a file or other resource using input from an upstream component, but it does not restrict or incorrectly restricts the resulting name.

CWE-642.name: External Control of Critical State Data

i18n.en: The product stores security-critical state information about its users, or the product itself, in a location that is accessible to unauthorized actors.

CWE-643.name: Improper Neutralization of Data within XPath Expressions ('XPath Injection')

i18n.en: The product uses external input to dynamically construct an XPath expression used to retrieve data from an XML database, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes that input. This allows an attacker to control the structure of the query.
i18n.ar: تغيير تعبير XPath عبر مدخل غير موثوق.

it.en: The attacker injects XPath syntax into a query over XML data, bypassing auth or reading nodes they shouldn't.
it.ar: يحقن المهاجم صيغة XPath في استعلام على بيانات XML، فيتجاوز المصادقة أو يقرأ عُقدًا لا يحق له.

CWE-644.name: Improper Neutralization of HTTP Headers for Scripting Syntax

i18n.en: The product does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes web scripting syntax in HTTP headers that can be used by web browser components that can process raw headers, such as Flash.

The product contains an account lockout protection mechanism, but the mechanism is too restrictive and can be triggered too easily, which allows attackers to deny service to legitimate users by causing their accounts to be locked out.

CWE-646.name: Reliance on File Name or Extension of Externally-Supplied File

i18n.en: The product allows a file to be uploaded, but it relies on the file name or extension of the file to determine the appropriate behaviors. This could be used by attackers to cause the file to be misclassified and processed in a dangerous fashion.

CWE-647.name: Use of Non-Canonical URL Paths for Authorization Decisions

i18n.en: The product defines policy namespaces and makes authorization decisions based on the assumption that a URL is canonical. This can allow a non-canonical URL to bypass the authorization.

The product does not conform to the API requirements for a function call that requires extra privileges. This could allow attackers to gain privileges by causing the function to be called incorrectly.

CWE-649.name: Reliance on Obfuscation or Encryption of Security-Relevant Inputs without Integrity Checking

i18n.en: The product uses obfuscation or encryption of inputs that should not be mutable by an external actor, but the product does not use integrity checks to detect if those inputs have been modified.

CWE-650.name: Trusting HTTP Permission Methods on the Server Side

i18n.en: The server contains a protection mechanism that assumes that any URI that is accessed using HTTP GET will not cause a state change to the associated resource. This might allow attackers to bypass intended access restrictions and conduct resource modification and deletion attacks, since some applications allow GET to modify state.

CWE-651.name: Exposure of WSDL File Containing Sensitive Information

i18n.en: The Web services architecture may require exposing a Web Service Definition Language (WSDL) file that contains information on the publicly accessible services and how callers of these services should interact with them (e.g. what parameters they expect and what types they return).

it.en: A web service leaks internal data structures in responses, handing the attacker a map of sensitive fields.
it.ar: تسرّب خدمة ويب هياكل بيانات داخلية في الاستجابات، فتسلّم المهاجم خريطة الحقول الحساسة.

CWE-652.name: Improper Neutralization of Data within XQuery Expressions ('XQuery Injection')

i18n.en: The product uses external input to dynamically construct an XQuery expression used to retrieve data from an XML database, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes that input. This allows an attacker to control the structure of the query.
The product does not properly compartmentalize or isolate functionality, processes, or resources that require different privilege levels, rights, or permissions.

CWE-654.name: Reliance on a Single Factor in a Security Decision

i18n.en: A protection mechanism relies exclusively, or to a large extent, on the evaluation of a single condition or the integrity of a single object or entity in order to make a decision about granting access to restricted resources or functionality.
The product has a protection mechanism that is too difficult or inconvenient to use, encouraging non-malicious users to disable or bypass the mechanism, whether by accident or on purpose.
The product uses a protection mechanism whose strength depends heavily on its obscurity, such that knowledge of its algorithms or key data is sufficient to defeat the mechanism.
The product violates well-established principles for secure design.

The product utilizes multiple threads, processes, components, or systems to allow temporary access to a shared resource that can only be exclusive to one process at a time, but it does not properly synchronize these actions, which might cause simultaneous accesses of this resource by multiple threads or processes.

ot.en: Two tasks touch the same variable without locking; an attacker (or bad timing) hits the race so the controller reads a half-written value and misacts.
ot.ar: مهمتان تلمسان المتغيّر نفسه دون قفل؛ يستغل المهاجم (أو توقيت سيئ) التسابق فيقرأ المتحكم قيمة نصف مكتوبة ويتصرّف خطأ.

it.en: A race on shared state lets an attacker interleave requests to corrupt data or bypass a check (e.g. double-spend).
it.ar: تسابق على حالة مشتركة يتيح للمهاجم تشابك الطلبات لإفساد البيانات أو تجاوز فحص (مثل الإنفاق المزدوج).

CWE-663.name: Use of a Non-reentrant Function in a Concurrent Context

i18n.en: The product calls a non-reentrant function in a concurrent context in which a competing code sequence (e.g. thread or signal handler) may have an opportunity to call the same function or otherwise influence its state.

CWE-664.name: Improper Control of a Resource Through its Lifetime

i18n.en: The product does not maintain or incorrectly maintains control over a resource throughout its lifetime of creation, use, and release.
i18n.ar: الإخفاق في التحكم السليم بمورد طوال دورة حياته.

i18n.en: The product does not initialize or incorrectly initializes a resource, which might leave the resource in an unexpected state when it is accessed or used.

CWE-666.name: Operation on Resource in Wrong Phase of Lifetime

i18n.en: The product performs an operation on a resource at the wrong phase of the resource's lifecycle, which can lead to unexpected behaviors.
The product does not properly acquire or release a lock on a resource, leading to unexpected resource state changes and behaviors.

CWE-668.name: Exposure of Resource to Wrong Sphere

i18n.en: The product exposes a resource to the wrong control sphere, providing unintended actors with inappropriate access to the resource.
i18n.ar: إتاحة مورد ضمن نطاق تحكّم غير مقصود.

i18n.en: The product does not properly transfer a resource/behavior to another sphere, or improperly imports a resource/behavior from another sphere, in a manner that provides unintended control over that resource.
The code contains a control flow path that does not reflect the algorithm that the path is intended to implement, leading to incorrect behavior any time this path is navigated.

CWE-671.name: Lack of Administrator Control over Security

i18n.en: The product uses security features in a way that prevents the product's administrator from tailoring security settings to reflect the environment in which the product is being used. This introduces resultant weaknesses or prevents it from operating at a level of security that is desired by the administrator.

CWE-672.name: Operation on a Resource after Expiration or Release

i18n.en: The product uses, accesses, or otherwise operates on a resource after that resource has been expired, released, or revoked.
The product does not prevent the definition of control spheres from external actors.
The product does not properly control the amount of recursion that takes place, consuming excessive resources, such as allocated memory or the program stack.

CWE-675.name: Multiple Operations on Resource in Single-Operation Context

i18n.en: The product performs the same operation on a resource two or more times, when the operation should only be applied once.
The product invokes a potentially dangerous function that could introduce a vulnerability if it is used incorrectly, but the function can also be used safely.
The product performs a calculation to determine how much memory to allocate, but an integer overflow can occur that causes less memory to be allocated than expected, leading to a buffer overflow.

When converting from one data type to another, such as long to integer, data can be omitted or translated in a way that produces unexpected values. If the resulting values are used in a sensitive context, then dangerous behaviors may occur.
The product performs a calculation that generates incorrect or unintended results that are later used in security-critical decisions or resource management.

CWE-683.name: Function Call With Incorrect Order of Arguments

i18n.en: The product calls a function, procedure, or routine, but the caller specifies the arguments in an incorrect order, leading to resultant weaknesses.
The code does not function according to its published specifications, potentially leading to incorrect usage.

CWE-685.name: Function Call With Incorrect Number of Arguments

i18n.en: The product calls a function, procedure, or routine, but the caller specifies too many arguments, or too few arguments, which may lead to undefined behavior and resultant weaknesses.

CWE-686.name: Function Call With Incorrect Argument Type

i18n.en: The product calls a function, procedure, or routine, but the caller specifies an argument that is the wrong data type, which may lead to resultant weaknesses.

CWE-687.name: Function Call With Incorrectly Specified Argument Value

i18n.en: The product calls a function, procedure, or routine, but the caller specifies an argument that contains the wrong value, which may lead to resultant weaknesses.

CWE-688.name: Function Call With Incorrect Variable or Reference as Argument

i18n.en: The product calls a function, procedure, or routine, but the caller specifies the wrong variable or reference as one of the arguments, which may lead to undefined behavior and resultant weaknesses.

CWE-689.name: Permission Race Condition During Resource Copy

i18n.en: The product, while copying or cloning a resource, does not set the resource's permissions or access control until the copy is complete, leaving the resource exposed to other spheres while the copy is taking place.

CWE-690.name: Unchecked Return Value to NULL Pointer Dereference

i18n.en: The product does not check for an error after calling a function that can return with a NULL pointer if the function fails, which leads to a resultant NULL pointer dereference.
The code does not sufficiently manage its control flow during execution, creating conditions in which the control flow can be modified in unexpected ways.
The product uses a denylist-based protection mechanism to defend against XSS attacks, but the denylist is incomplete, allowing XSS variants to succeed.
The product does not use or incorrectly uses a protection mechanism that provides sufficient defense against directed attacks against the product.

it.en: A protection mechanism is missing or bypassable, so the attacker simply goes around the control that should stop them.
it.ar: آلية حماية غائبة أو قابلة للتجاوز، فيلتفّ المهاجم ببساطة حول الضابط الذي يُفترض أن يوقفه.

CWE-694.name: Use of Multiple Resources with Duplicate Identifier

i18n.en: The product uses multiple resources that can have the same identifier, in a context in which unique identifiers are required.
The product uses low-level functionality that is explicitly prohibited by the framework or specification under which the product is supposed to operate.
The product performs multiple related behaviors, but the behaviors are performed in the wrong order in ways that may produce resultant weaknesses.
The product compares two entities in a security-relevant context, but the comparison is incorrect.
i18n.ar: مقارنة غير صحيحة بين قيم أو كائنات.

i18n.en: The web application sends a redirect to another location, but instead of exiting, it executes additional code.

CWE-703.name: Improper Check or Handling of Exceptional Conditions

i18n.en: The product does not properly anticipate or handle exceptional conditions that rarely occur during normal operation of the product.
The product does not correctly convert an object, resource, or structure from one type to a different type.

ot.en: An unsafe type conversion (e.g. signed/unsigned or truncation) flips a value, so a safe-looking number becomes a dangerous one in the controller.
ot.ar: تحويل نوع غير آمن (مثل إشارة/بدون إشارة أو اقتطاع) يقلب قيمة، فيصبح رقم يبدو آمنًا خطِرًا في المتحكم.

it.en: A bad cast turns one value into another (truncation/sign flip), letting an attacker slip past a size or range check.
it.ar: تحويل سيئ يقلب قيمة إلى أخرى (اقتطاع/قلب إشارة)، فيتسلّل المهاجم متجاوزًا فحص حجم أو نطاق.

i18n.en: The product does not properly return control flow to the proper location after it has completed a task or detected an unusual condition.

CWE-706.name: Use of Incorrectly-Resolved Name or Reference

i18n.en: The product uses a name or reference to access a resource, but the name/reference resolves to a resource that is outside of the intended control sphere.
i18n.ar: استخدام اسم يُحَل بشكل غير صحيح إلى مورد غير مقصود.

i18n.en: The product does not ensure or incorrectly ensures that structured messages or data are well-formed and that certain security properties are met before being read from an upstream component or sent to a downstream component.
i18n.ar: الإخفاق في تنظيف أو التحقق من المدخلات/المخرجات بشكل عام.

i18n.en: The product assigns an owner to a resource, but the owner is outside of the intended control sphere.
The product does not follow certain coding rules for development, which can lead to resultant weaknesses or increase the severity of the associated vulnerabilities.

it.en: Not following secure-coding practice isn't one attack, but it leaves the gaps attackers chain together.
it.ar: عدم اتباع ممارسات الترميز الآمن ليس هجومًا واحدًا، لكنه يترك الثغرات التي يربطها المهاجمون معًا.

CWE-732.name: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource

i18n.en: The product specifies permissions for a security-critical resource in a way that allows that resource to be read or modified by unintended actors.

it.en: Over-broad file/resource permissions let any local user (or a low-priv attacker) read or change what should be protected.
it.ar: صلاحيات ملفات/موارد واسعة تتيح لأي مستخدم محلي (أو مهاجم منخفض الصلاحية) قراءة أو تغيير ما يجب حمايته.

CWE-733.name: Compiler Optimization Removal or Modification of Security-critical Code

i18n.en: The developer builds a security-critical protection mechanism into the software, but the compiler optimizes the program such that the mechanism is removed or modified.

The product provides an Applications Programming Interface (API) or similar interface for interaction with external actors, but the interface includes a dangerous method or function that is not properly restricted.

CWE-754.name: Improper Check for Unusual or Exceptional Conditions

i18n.en: The product does not check or incorrectly checks for unusual or exceptional conditions that are not expected to occur frequently during day to day operation of the product.
The product does not handle or incorrectly handles an exceptional condition.

it.en: Poor error handling exposes internals or leaves the system in an unsafe state the attacker exploits.
it.ar: معالجة أخطاء رديئة تكشف الداخل أو تترك النظام في حالة غير آمنة يستغلها المهاجم.

i18n.en: The product does not return custom error pages to the user, possibly exposing sensitive information.

CWE-757.name: Selection of Less-Secure Algorithm During Negotiation ('Algorithm Downgrade')

i18n.en: A protocol or its implementation supports interaction between multiple actors and allows those actors to negotiate which algorithm should be used as a protection mechanism such as encryption or authentication, but it does not select the strongest algorithm that is available to both parties.

CWE-758.name: Reliance on Undefined, Unspecified, or Implementation-Defined Behavior

i18n.en: The product uses an API function, data structure, or other entity in a way that relies on properties that are not always guaranteed to hold for that entity.

CWE-759.name: Use of a One-Way Hash without a Salt

i18n.en: The product uses a one-way cryptographic hash against an input that should not be reversible, such as a password, but the product does not also use a salt as part of the input.

CWE-760.name: Use of a One-Way Hash with a Predictable Salt

i18n.en: The product uses a one-way cryptographic hash against an input that should not be reversible, such as a password, but the product uses a predictable salt as part of the input.

CWE-761.name: Free of Pointer not at Start of Buffer

i18n.en: The product calls free() on a pointer to a memory resource that was allocated on the heap, but the pointer is not at the start of the buffer.
The product attempts to return a memory resource to the system, but it calls a release function that is not compatible with the function that was originally used to allocate that resource.

CWE-763.name: Release of Invalid Pointer or Reference

i18n.en: The product attempts to return a memory resource to the system, but it calls the wrong release function or calls the appropriate release function incorrectly.

CWE-764.name: Multiple Locks of a Critical Resource

i18n.en: The product locks a critical resource more times than intended, leading to an unexpected state in the system.

CWE-765.name: Multiple Unlocks of a Critical Resource

i18n.en: The product unlocks a critical resource more times than intended, leading to an unexpected state in the system.
The product declares a critical variable, field, or member to be public when intended security policy requires it to be private.

CWE-767.name: Access to Critical Private Variable via Public Method

i18n.en: The product defines a public method that reads or modifies a private variable.

The product contains a conditional statement with multiple logical expressions in which one of the non-leading expressions may produce side effects. This may lead to an unexpected state in the program after the execution of the conditional, because short-circuiting logic may prevent the side effects from occurring.
This entry has been deprecated because it was a duplicate of CWE-774. All content has been transferred to CWE-774.

CWE-770.name: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

i18n.en: The product allocates a reusable resource or group of resources on behalf of an actor without imposing any intended restrictions on the size or number of resources that can be allocated.

it.en: No limit on a resource (connections, memory, items) lets the attacker request until the service is exhausted.
it.ar: لا حدّ لمورد (اتصالات، ذاكرة، عناصر) يتيح للمهاجم الطلب حتى تُستنزف الخدمة.

ot.en: An unbounded allocation/queue in the controller lets a flood of network data exhaust memory and fault the PLC.
ot.ar: حجز/طابور غير محدود في المتحكم يتيح لسيل بيانات شبكية استنزاف الذاكرة وتعطيل الـPLC.

CWE-771.name: Missing Reference to Active Allocated Resource

i18n.en: The product does not properly maintain a reference to a resource that has been allocated, which prevents the resource from being reclaimed.

CWE-772.name: Missing Release of Resource after Effective Lifetime

i18n.en: The product does not release a resource after its effective lifetime has ended, i.e., after the resource is no longer needed.

CWE-773.name: Missing Reference to Active File Descriptor or Handle

i18n.en: The product does not properly maintain references to a file descriptor or handle, which prevents that file descriptor/handle from being reclaimed.

CWE-774.name: Allocation of File Descriptors or Handles Without Limits or Throttling

i18n.en: The product allocates file descriptors or handles on behalf of an actor without imposing any restrictions on how many descriptors can be allocated, in violation of the intended security policy for that actor.

CWE-775.name: Missing Release of File Descriptor or Handle after Effective Lifetime

i18n.en: The product does not release a file descriptor or handle after its effective lifetime has ended, i.e., after the file descriptor/handle is no longer needed.

CWE-776.name: Improper Restriction of Recursive Entity References in DTDs ('XML Entity Expansion')

i18n.en: The product uses XML documents and allows their structure to be defined with a Document Type Definition (DTD), but it does not properly control the number of recursive definitions of entities.

it.en: The attacker sends XML with nested entities that expand exponentially (billion laughs), exhausting memory.
it.ar: يرسل المهاجم XML بكيانات متداخلة تتمدد أُسّيًّا (مليار ضحكة)، فيستنزف الذاكرة.

i18n.en: The product uses a regular expression to perform neutralization, but the regular expression is not anchored and may allow malicious or malformed data to slip through.
When a security-critical event occurs, the product either does not record the event or omits important details about the event when logging it.

it.en: Without proper logging, the attacker's actions leave no trace, so a breach goes undetected and un-investigable.
it.ar: بلا تسجيل سليم، لا تترك أفعال المهاجم أثرًا، فيمرّ الاختراق دون كشف أو تحقيق.

i18n.en: The product logs too much information, making log files hard to process and possibly hindering recovery efforts or forensic analysis after an attack.

CWE-780.name: Use of RSA Algorithm without OAEP

i18n.en: The product uses the RSA algorithm but does not incorporate Optimal Asymmetric Encryption Padding (OAEP), which might weaken the encryption.

CWE-781.name: Improper Address Validation in IOCTL with METHOD_NEITHER I/O Control Code

i18n.en: The product defines an IOCTL that uses METHOD_NEITHER for I/O, but it does not validate or incorrectly validates the addresses that are provided.

CWE-782.name: Exposed IOCTL with Insufficient Access Control

i18n.en: The product implements an IOCTL with functionality that should be restricted, but it does not properly enforce access control for the IOCTL.
The product uses an expression in which operator precedence causes incorrect logic to be used.

CWE-784.name: Reliance on Cookies without Validation and Integrity Checking in a Security Decision

i18n.en: The product uses a protection mechanism that relies on the existence or values of a cookie, but it does not properly ensure that the cookie is valid for the associated user.

CWE-785.name: Use of Path Manipulation Function without Maximum-sized Buffer

i18n.en: The product invokes a function for normalizing paths or file names, but it provides an output buffer that is smaller than the maximum possible size, such as PATH_MAX.

CWE-786.name: Access of Memory Location Before Start of Buffer

i18n.en: The product reads or writes to a buffer using an index or pointer that references a memory location prior to the beginning of the buffer.

ot.en: A write before the start of a buffer corrupts memory just below it, so the controller behaves unpredictably.
ot.ar: كتابة قبل بداية المخزن تُفسد الذاكرة أسفله مباشرة، فيتصرّف المتحكم بشكل غير متوقع.

it.en: Writing before a buffer's start overwrites adjacent memory, which an attacker shapes to corrupt control data.
it.ar: الكتابة قبل بداية المخزن تطمس ذاكرة مجاورة يشكّلها المهاجم لإفساد بيانات التحكم.

i18n.en: The product writes data past the end, or before the beginning, of the intended buffer.

it.en: The attacker writes past the end of a buffer, overwriting memory to crash the program or run their code (RCE).
it.ar: يكتب المهاجم بعد نهاية المخزن، فيطمس الذاكرة لتعطيل البرنامج أو تشغيل شيفرته (تنفيذ عن بُعد).

ot.en: An oversized value writes past an array in the controller, overwriting setpoints or return addresses and misfiring outputs.
ot.ar: قيمة كبيرة تكتب بعد مصفوفة في المتحكم، فتطمس القيم المحددة أو عناوين العودة وتُطلق مخرجات خاطئة.

CWE-788.name: Access of Memory Location After End of Buffer

i18n.en: The product reads or writes to a buffer using an index or pointer that references a memory location after the end of the buffer.

ot.en: Access just past the end of a buffer reads/writes wrong memory, leaking data or destabilizing the controller.
ot.ar: وصول بعد نهاية المخزن مباشرة يقرأ/يكتب ذاكرة خاطئة، فيسرّب بيانات أو يزعزع المتحكم.

it.en: Reading/writing just past a buffer leaks adjacent memory (e.g. keys) or corrupts state for an attacker.
it.ar: القراءة/الكتابة بعد المخزن مباشرة تسرّب ذاكرة مجاورة (مثل المفاتيح) أو تُفسد الحالة لصالح المهاجم.

CWE-789.name: Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value

i18n.en: The product allocates memory based on an untrusted, large size value, but it does not ensure that the size is within expected limits, allowing arbitrary amounts of memory to be allocated.
The product receives data from an upstream component, but does not filter or incorrectly filters special elements before sending it to a downstream component.
The product receives data from an upstream component, but does not completely filter special elements before sending it to a downstream component.

CWE-792.name: Incomplete Filtering of One or More Instances of Special Elements

i18n.en: The product receives data from an upstream component, but does not completely filter one or more instances of special elements before sending it to a downstream component.

CWE-793.name: Only Filtering One Instance of a Special Element

i18n.en: The product receives data from an upstream component, but only filters a single instance of a special element before sending it to a downstream component.

CWE-794.name: Incomplete Filtering of Multiple Instances of Special Elements

i18n.en: The product receives data from an upstream component, but does not filter all instances of a special element before sending it to a downstream component.

CWE-795.name: Only Filtering Special Elements at a Specified Location

i18n.en: The product receives data from an upstream component, but only accounts for special elements at a specified location, thereby missing remaining special elements that may exist before sending it to a downstream component.

CWE-796.name: Only Filtering Special Elements Relative to a Marker

i18n.en: The product receives data from an upstream component, but only accounts for special elements positioned relative to a marker (e.g. "at the beginning/end of a string; the second argument"), thereby missing remaining special elements that may exist before sending it to a downstream component.

CWE-797.name: Only Filtering Special Elements at an Absolute Position

i18n.en: The product receives data from an upstream component, but only accounts for special elements at an absolute position (e.g. "byte number 10"), thereby missing remaining special elements that may exist before sending it to a downstream component.
The product contains hard-coded credentials, such as a password or cryptographic key.

it.en: A password/key is written right in the code; anyone who reads the source or binary logs in as the app.
it.ar: كلمة مرور/مفتاح مكتوب في الشيفرة مباشرة؛ فمن يقرأ المصدر أو الملف التنفيذي يدخل كالتطبيق.

ot.en: A hard-coded controller/HMI credential is the same on every site, so reading one project file unlocks the whole fleet.
ot.ar: بيانات اعتماد متحكم/HMI مثبّتة في الشيفرة تكون نفسها بكل موقع، فقراءة ملف مشروع واحد تفتح الأسطول كله.

i18n.en: The product does not properly limit the number or frequency of interactions that it has with an actor, such as the number of incoming requests.

it.en: No control over how often an action runs lets the attacker hammer it (e.g. OTP requests), enabling abuse or DoS.
it.ar: غياب التحكم في تكرار الإجراء يتيح للمهاجم قصفه (مثل طلبات OTP)، ما يمكّن من إساءة الاستخدام أو حجب الخدمة.

i18n.en: The product uses a CAPTCHA challenge, but the challenge can be guessed or automatically recognized by a non-human actor.

CWE-805.name: Buffer Access with Incorrect Length Value

i18n.en: The product uses a sequential operation to read or write a buffer, but it uses an incorrect length value that causes it to access memory that is outside of the bounds of the buffer.

CWE-806.name: Buffer Access Using Size of Source Buffer

i18n.en: The product uses the size of a source buffer when reading from or writing to a destination buffer, which may cause it to access memory that is outside of the bounds of the buffer.

CWE-807.name: Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision

i18n.en: The product uses a protection mechanism that relies on the existence or values of an input, but the input can be modified by an untrusted actor in a way that bypasses the protection mechanism.

it.en: A security decision relies on input the attacker controls (a header/cookie), so they just set it to 'admin=true'.
it.ar: قرار أمني يعتمد على مُدخل يتحكم به المهاجم (ترويسة/ملف ارتباط)، فيضبطه ببساطة إلى 'admin=true'.

ot.en: An access/safety decision trusts a wire value the attacker can spoof, so they bypass an interlock by faking the input.
ot.ar: قرار وصول/سلامة يثق بقيمة شبكية يستطيع المهاجم تزويرها، فيتجاوز تعشيقة أمان بتزييف المُدخل.

i18n.en: The product utilizes a shared resource in a concurrent manner but does not attempt to synchronize access to the resource.
The product utilizes a shared resource in a concurrent manner, but it does not correctly synchronize access to the resource.
The product obtains a value from an untrusted source, converts this value to a pointer, and dereferences the resulting pointer.
The product performs pointer arithmetic on a valid pointer, but it uses an offset that can point outside of the intended range of valid memory locations for the resulting pointer.
The product accesses or uses a pointer that has not been initialized.
The product dereferences a pointer that contains a location for memory that was previously valid, but is no longer valid.

CWE-826.name: Premature Release of Resource During Expected Lifetime

i18n.en: The product releases a resource that is still intended to be used by itself or another actor.

CWE-827.name: Improper Control of Document Type Definition

i18n.en: The product does not restrict a reference to a Document Type Definition (DTD) to the intended control sphere. This might allow attackers to reference arbitrary DTDs, possibly causing the product to expose files, consume excessive system resources, or execute arbitrary http requests on behalf of the attacker.

CWE-828.name: Signal Handler with Functionality that is not Asynchronous-Safe

i18n.en: The product defines a signal handler that contains code sequences that are not asynchronous-safe, i.e., the functionality is not reentrant, or it can be interrupted.

CWE-829.name: Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere

i18n.en: The product imports, requires, or includes executable functionality (such as a library) from a source that is outside of the intended control sphere.

CWE-830.name: Inclusion of Web Functionality from an Untrusted Source

i18n.en: The product includes web functionality (such as a web widget) from another domain, which causes it to operate within the domain of the product, potentially granting total access and control of the product to the untrusted source.

CWE-831.name: Signal Handler Function Associated with Multiple Signals

i18n.en: The product defines a function that is used as a handler for more than one signal.

CWE-832.name: Unlock of a Resource that is not Locked

i18n.en: The product attempts to unlock a resource that is not locked.
The product contains multiple threads or executable segments that are waiting for each other to release a necessary lock, resulting in deadlock.
The product performs an iteration or loop without sufficiently limiting the number of times that the loop is executed.

CWE-835.name: Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition ('Infinite Loop')

i18n.en: The product contains an iteration or loop with an exit condition that cannot be reached, i.e., an infinite loop.

it.en: The attacker sends input that traps the program in an endless loop, pinning the CPU and denying service.
it.ar: يرسل المهاجم مُدخلًا يحبس البرنامج في حلقة لا نهائية، فيثبّت المعالج ويحجب الخدمة.

ot.en: A loop with no reachable exit hangs the controller's scan, tripping the watchdog and stopping the process.
ot.ar: حلقة بلا مخرج قابل للوصول تعلّق دورة المتحكم، فتُطلق المراقب وتوقف العملية.

CWE-836.name: Use of Password Hash Instead of Password for Authentication

i18n.en: The product records password hashes in a data store, receives a hash of a password from a client, and compares the supplied hash to the hash obtained from the data store.

CWE-837.name: Improper Enforcement of a Single, Unique Action

i18n.en: The product requires that an actor should only be able to perform an action once, or to have only one unique action, but the product does not enforce or improperly enforces this restriction.

it.en: A check that should run once can be replayed, so the attacker reuses a one-time token or coupon many times.
it.ar: فحص يُفترض أن يجري مرة واحدة يمكن إعادته، فيعيد المهاجم استخدام رمز/قسيمة لمرة واحدة مرارًا.

i18n.en: The product uses or specifies an encoding when generating output to a downstream component, but the specified encoding is not the same as the encoding that is expected by the downstream component.

CWE-839.name: Numeric Range Comparison Without Minimum Check

i18n.en: The product checks a value to ensure that it is less than or equal to a maximum, but it does not also verify that the value is greater than or equal to the minimum.
The product supports a session in which more than one behavior must be performed by an actor, but it does not properly ensure that the actor performs the behaviors in the required sequence.

CWE-842.name: Placement of User into Incorrect Group

i18n.en: The product or the administrator places a user into an incorrect group.

CWE-843.name: Access of Resource Using Incompatible Type ('Type Confusion')

i18n.en: The product allocates or initializes a resource such as a pointer, object, or variable using one type, but it later accesses that resource using a type that is incompatible with the original type.
The product does not perform an authorization check when an actor attempts to access a resource or perform an action.

it.en: An action has no authorization check, so a normal user calls the admin function and it just works.
it.ar: إجراء بلا فحص تفويض، فيستدعي مستخدم عادي دالة الإدارة فتعمل ببساطة.

i18n.en: The product performs an authorization check when an actor attempts to access a resource or perform an action, but it does not correctly perform the check.
The product uses or accesses a resource that has not been initialized.
The product does not initialize a critical resource.
The product uses or accesses a file descriptor after it has been closed.
The product uses a reference count to manage a resource, but it does not update or incorrectly updates the reference count.

The product contains functionality that is not documented, not part of the specification, and not accessible through an interface or command sequence that is obvious to the product's users or administrators.

it.en: A hidden feature (backdoor) shipped in the product lets whoever knows it bypass all the normal controls.
it.ar: ميزة مخفية (باب خلفي) شُحنت في المنتج تتيح لمن يعرفها تجاوز كل الضوابط العادية.

CWE-913.name: Improper Control of Dynamically-Managed Code Resources

i18n.en: The product does not properly restrict reading from or writing to dynamically-managed code resources such as variables, objects, classes, attributes, functions, or executable instructions or statements.
i18n.ar: تأثير بيانات غير موثوقة على شيفرة أو كائنات تُدار ديناميكياً.

i18n.en: The product does not properly restrict reading from or writing to dynamically-identified variables.

CWE-915.name: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes
